blocks.content: Sedimentary rocks cover nearly 75 percent of the Earth's continental surface, preserving invaluable records of ancient environments and prehistoric life.

rows: Compaction and cementation of physical rock fragments derived from weathering
Direct chemical precipitation of dissolved minerals as water evaporates
Rock Salt (Halite), Gypsum, Flint, Potash, Dolomite
Accumulation and thermal conversion of animal bones/shells or plant matter
Coal, Chalk, Fossiliferous Limestone, Peat, Lignite

items: Fossils are exclusively preserved in sedimentary rocks; extreme heat and pressure in igneous and metamorphic rocks destroy organic remains.
Differentiate Conglomerate (composed of rounded fragments due to transport action) from Breccia (composed of sharp, angular fragments).
Limestone can be classified as both organic (fossiliferous chalk/coral reef) and chemical (travertine) based on its environmental origin.
Remember the sequence of coal formation by increasing carbon content and heat value: Peat -> Lignite -> Bituminous -> Anthracite.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Clastic sedimentary rocks are formed from the accumulation, compaction, and cementation of pre-existing rock fragments and mineral grains.
Chemically formed sedimentary rocks originate from the precipitation of dissolved minerals out of water solutions during evaporation.
Organically formed sedimentary rocks develop from the accumulated debris of dead plants and marine organisms over geological time scales.
Lithification is the dual process of compaction under heavy pressure and cementation by precipitating minerals that converts loose sediment into solid rock.
Sedimentary rocks are uniquely characterized by stratification (layering) and are the primary source of fossil evidence on Earth.
